levels.title: Art History in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the big eras of art from cave paintings to today.

levels.title: What Counts as Art?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why people have disagreed about what counts as art.

levels.title: The Artist's Toolkit
levels.objective: After this level you can name the basic elements of art: line, shape, color, texture and space.

levels.title: How Color Works
levels.objective: After this level you can explain primary and complementary colors and how artists use them.

levels.title: The First Artists
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the oldest known cave art and how it was made.

levels.title: Lascaux and Chauvet
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the animal paintings in the caves of Lascaux and Chauvet.

levels.title: The First Sculptures
levels.objective: After this level you can describe early carved figures and what they may have meant.

levels.title: Stonehenge and Great Stones
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what monuments like Stonehenge show about early societies.

levels.title: Why Early People Made Art
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the main ideas about why early humans made art.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The First Artists
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the earliest known art and the main ideas about why it was made.

levels.title: Mesopotamia
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Mesopotamian art, from stepped temples to carved seals.

levels.title: The Rules of Egyptian Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the rules that kept Egyptian art so consistent for 3,000 years.

levels.title: Art for the Afterlife
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Egyptians filled their tombs with art.

levels.title: Greek Vases
levels.objective: After this level you can explain black-figure and red-figure vase painting.

levels.title: Greek Sculpture
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Greek sculptors moved from stiff figures to lifelike bodies.

levels.title: Greek Temples
levels.objective: After this level you can name the three Greek column styles and describe the Parthenon.

levels.title: Roman Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Roman art borrowed from Greece and what it added.

levels.title: Mosaics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how mosaics are made and where they flourished.

levels.title: Early Art of China and India
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Terracotta Army and early Buddhist sculpture.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Ancient Worlds
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the art of Egypt, Greece, Rome and early Asia.

levels.title: Byzantine Art
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Byzantine icons and gold-backed mosaics.

levels.title: Islamic Art and Pattern
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Islamic art so often uses geometry, pattern and calligraphy.

levels.title: The Alhambra and Great Mosques
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the architecture of the Alhambra and the great mosques.

levels.title: Illuminated Manuscripts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how medieval scribes made illuminated manuscripts.

levels.title: Romanesque Churches
levels.objective: After this level you can describe thick-walled Romanesque churches and their round arches.

levels.title: Gothic Cathedrals
levels.objective: After this level you can explain pointed arches and flying buttresses and why Gothic churches soar.

levels.title: Stained Glass
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how stained glass windows were made and what they taught.

levels.title: Giotto
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Giotto made painted figures look solid and human.

levels.title: Chinese Landscape Painting
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Chinese painters used ink to capture mountains and mist.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Faith and Empire
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how faith shaped art from Byzantium to Gothic Europe and the Islamic world.

levels.title: What Was the Renaissance?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Renaissance's rebirth meant and why it began in Florence.

levels.title: Perspective
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how linear perspective makes a flat picture look deep.

levels.title: Brunelleschi's Dome
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Brunelleschi built Florence's great dome.

levels.title: Patrons and the Medici
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how rich patrons like the Medici paid for Renaissance art.

levels.title: Leonardo da Vinci
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Leonardo's paintings and his notebooks.

levels.title: Michelangelo
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

levels.title: Raphael and the High Renaissance
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what made High Renaissance painting feel balanced and calm.

levels.title: Oil Paint and the North
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Flemish painters like van Eyck used oil paint for fine detail.

levels.title: Prints and the Printing Press
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how printing spread images through woodcuts and engravings.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Renaissance
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what changed in art during the Renaissance and who led the change.

levels.title: Baroque Drama
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Baroque art used movement and emotion to grab the viewer.

levels.title: Caravaggio and Light
levels.objective: After this level you can explain chiaroscuro and Caravaggio's dramatic lighting.

levels.title: Bernini
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Bernini's sculpture and his square at St. Peter's.

levels.title: Rembrandt
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Rembrandt used light and why he painted so many self-portraits.

levels.title: The Dutch Golden Age
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Dutch painters sold everyday scenes and still lifes.

levels.title: Vermeer
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Vermeer's quiet interiors and how he painted light.

levels.title: Velázquez
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Las Meninas still puzzles viewers.

levels.title: Rococo
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the playful, pastel Rococo style.

levels.title: Neoclassicism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why artists turned back to Greece and Rome in the late 1700s.

levels.title: Milestone: From Caves to Classics
levels.objective: After this level you can connect art from the caves to Neoclassicism into one story.

levels.title: Romanticism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Romantic artists painted storms, feeling and the sublime.

levels.title: Goya
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Goya's path from court painter to dark visions.

levels.title: Landscape Painting
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Turner and Constable made landscape a serious subject.

levels.title: Realism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why Realists painted ordinary workers instead of heroes.

levels.title: Photography Arrives
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how photography changed what painters thought painting was for.

levels.title: Impressionism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Impressionists painted light and passing moments outdoors.

levels.title: Monet
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Monet's series paintings and his water lilies.

levels.title: Degas and Modern Life
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how Degas captured dancers and city life.

levels.title: Morisot and Cassatt
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the work of Berthe Morisot and Mary Cassatt and what they chose to paint.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Revolutions in Art
levels.objective: After this level you can trace art from Romanticism through Realism to Impressionism.

levels.title: Post-Impressionism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Cézanne, Gauguin and Seurat pushed past Impressionism.

levels.title: Van Gogh
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Van Gogh's brushwork, his colors and his life.

levels.title: Seurat and Pointillism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how dots of pure color blend in the eye.

levels.title: Art Nouveau
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Art Nouveau's flowing lines and plant forms.

levels.title: Expressionism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Expressionists bent color and form to show feeling.

levels.title: Picasso and Cubism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Cubism showed objects from many angles at once.

levels.title: Abstract Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Kandinsky and Mondrian left recognizable subjects behind.

levels.title: Dada
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Dada's protest against art and Duchamp's ready-mades.

levels.title: Surrealism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the Surrealists painted dreams, from Dalí to Magritte.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Breaking the Rules
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how modern artists moved from Post-Impressionism to abstraction and Surrealism.

levels.title: Japanese Woodblock Prints
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how ukiyo-e prints were made, including Hokusai's Great Wave.

levels.title: Japan's Influence on the West
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Japanese prints inspired the Impressionists.

levels.title: Chinese Calligraphy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why calligraphy is a major art form in China.

levels.title: Art of Africa
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Benin Bronzes and masks and the roles they played.

levels.title: African Art and Modernism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how African sculpture influenced Picasso and other modern artists.

levels.title: Aboriginal Art
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Aboriginal rock art and dot painting and the stories they carry.

levels.title: Art of the Americas
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Maya, Aztec and Inca art and building.

levels.title: Mexican Muralism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Diego Rivera and others painted history on public walls.

levels.title: Frida Kahlo
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Kahlo's self-portraits and the symbols in them.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Art Around the World
levels.objective: After this level you can compare art traditions from Japan, China, Africa, Australia and the Americas.

levels.title: Abstract Expressionism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Pollock and Rothko made the act of painting the subject.

levels.title: Pop Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Pop Art borrowed from ads, comics and celebrity.

levels.title: Warhol
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Warhol's repeated images and his studio, the Factory.

levels.title: Minimalism
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Minimalism's plain shapes and industrial materials.

levels.title: Conceptual Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain art where the idea matters more than the object.

levels.title: Photography as Art
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how photographers like Ansel Adams made photography a fine art.

levels.title: Land Art and Installations
levels.objective: After this level you can describe art made from landscapes and from whole rooms.

levels.title: Street Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how graffiti and street art moved from walls into galleries.

levels.title: Art and Money
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why a few artworks sell for hundreds of millions of dollars.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Modern and Contemporary
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the main movements in art since 1945.

levels.title: How to Read a Painting
levels.objective: After this level you can use a simple method to look closely at any painting.

levels.title: Composition
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how artists guide your eye with balance, lines and a focal point.

levels.title: Symbols in Art
levels.objective: After this level you can decode common symbols like skulls, lilies and dogs in older paintings.

levels.title: Museums
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how museums began and what they do today.

levels.title: Restoration
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how conservators clean and repair old art.

levels.title: Forgery
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how famous forgeries were made and caught.

levels.title: Stolen Art
levels.objective: After this level you can describe famous art thefts, including the Mona Lisa in 1911.

levels.title: Digital Art
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how computers and screens have changed the way art is made.

levels.title: Why Art Lasts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why some art stays meaningful for centuries.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: Art History
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of Art History Levels 1–99 across the whole tree.
